content.value_statement: Agents often forget useful context and repeat work across sessions. This skill gives practical memory patterns for retrieval, storage, chunking, decay, and safe user filtering.
actual_capabilities: Explains semantic, episodic, and procedural memory using the CoALA framework.
Compares vector stores such as Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, ChromaDB, and pgvector.
Provides implementation patterns for LangMem, Pinecone, Qdrant, and ChromaDB memory flows.
Guides chunking strategy, contextual chunking, hybrid search, reranking, and metadata filtering.
Identifies sharp edges such as stale memories, missing user filters, context overflow, and model mismatch.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance and examples, not a deployed memory service.
Code samples require dependency setup, credentials, testing, and privacy review before production use.
It does not benchmark embedding models or vector databases for a specific workload.
It is not a substitute for legal review of user data retention and consent requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan persistent agent memory
use_cases.description: Design long-term memory that stores useful facts, events, and workflows without overloading the context window.

use_cases.title: Choose retrieval infrastructure
use_cases.description: Compare vector store options and select metadata filtering, hybrid search, and reranking patterns for the workload.

use_cases.title: Audit memory failure modes
use_cases.description: Review memory designs for stale data, missing user isolation, bad chunking, and mismatched embedding models.

prompt_templates.title: Map memory types
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my agent idea and map what belongs in semantic, episodic, and procedural memory. Include what should stay only in short-term context.

prompt_templates.title: Select a vector store
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, ChromaDB, and pgvector for my agent memory workload. Recommend one option and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design retrieval flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a retrieval flow for user-specific agent memory. Include chunking, metadata filters, hybrid search, reranking, and a context budget.

prompt_templates.title: Review production risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this agent memory design for stale memories, conflicting preferences, missing user isolation, embedding model migration risk, and context overflow.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to add memory to a support agent.
output: A memory architecture split into user profile facts, past support episodes, and reusable support procedures.
A retrieval plan that filters by user, issue type, and recency before adding memories to the prompt.
A short list of risks covering consent, stale preferences, and context budget limits.

output_examples.input: A team needs to choose a vector store for agent memories.
output: A comparison of managed and self-hosted options based on scale, filtering, latency, cost, and operational effort.
A recommendation for the best fit, plus a fallback option for prototyping or smaller deployments.

output_examples.input: An existing memory system retrieves irrelevant or conflicting results.
output: A diagnosis of weak chunking, missing metadata filters, stale memory handling, and embedding model mismatch.
A prioritized repair plan using user filters, temporal scoring, conflict checks, and retrieval evaluation.

best_practices: Filter memory retrieval by user, memory type, and time before ranking by semantic similarity.
Test chunk sizes and retrieval accuracy with representative queries before production use.
Track embedding model versions and plan migrations before changing providers or model families.
anti_patterns: Storing every interaction forever without decay, consent, or relevance scoring.
Using semantic similarity alone for private or user-specific memories.
Mixing embedding models for stored documents and live queries without migration controls.

faq.question: What kind of memory does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers short-term context, long-term vector storage, and semantic, episodic, and procedural memory patterns.

faq.question: Does it build a memory database automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples that developers must adapt, test, and deploy.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-agnostic and can support planning work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it recommend one vector database?
faq.answer: No. It explains tradeoffs across Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, ChromaDB, and pgvector.

faq.question: How does it address privacy?
faq.answer: It emphasizes user filtering, metadata controls, memory decay, and careful review before storing personal data.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when designing agents that need memory across sessions, retrieval from past events, or durable user preferences.
